primary_diagnosis_treated: Acute coronary syndrome (type 1 NSTEMI) with chronic kidney disease stage 5, alcoholic liver disease, and heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia
nice_guideline_used: CG126 / NG185 (ACS), NG106 (Heart failure), NG203 (CKD), NG136 (Lipid management)

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of cardiovascular events after ACS
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends lifelong aspirin for all IHD patients

medications.purpose: Dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI for NSTEMI
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends prasugrel or ticagrelor for 12 months after ACS

medications.dose: Initial bolus 70 U/kg IV, then infusion 15 U/kg/h titrated to aPTT 1.5–2.5× control
medications.duration: In‑hospital until discharge or definitive revascularisation
medications.purpose: Acute anticoagulation during NSTEMI (preferred over LMWH in eGFR < 30)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 advises anticoagulation during ACS; UFH is recommended when renal function is severely impaired

medications.duration: Lifelong – review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Intensive LDL‑C lowering for secondary prevention and FH
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG136 recommends high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20‑40 mg) for all IHD patients and FH

medications.duration: Lifelong – review LDL‑C at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Further LDL‑C reduction because LDL remains > 100 mg/dL despite high‑intensity statin and FH
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 (2022) recommends PCSK9‑i for FH or very high LDL when statin alone insufficient

medications.duration: 12 months (or until dual antiplatelet therapy completed)
medications.purpose: Gastro‑protection to reduce upper‑GI bleed risk with dual antiplatelet therapy
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 advises PPI co‑prescription with DAPT in high‑risk patients

medications.dose: 3.125 mg orally twice daily, titrate every 2 weeks to target HR <60 bpm (max 25 mg BID as tolerated)
medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate over 6–8 weeks then review annually
medications.purpose: Beta‑blockade for post‑MI cardioprotection and angina; chosen for hepatic clearance (safe in eGFR < 30)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 recommends carvedilol or bisoprolol as first‑line beta‑blocker in HFrEF/ post‑MI patients

medications.dose: 5 mg orally once daily (reduce from prior dose if higher)

medications.purpose: Cardioprotective ACE‑I for post‑MI and hypertension; dose reduced for eGFR = 9.5 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 and NG203 recommend ACE‑I for IHD and CKD, with dose adjustment in severe renal impairment

medications.purpose: Blood pressure control; remains appropriate after beta‑blocker optimisation
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 lists CCB as second‑line anti‑anginal/add‑on antihypertensive

medications.duration: Lifelong – monitor electrolytes and renal function
medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive; low dose acceptable despite eGFR < 30
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends thiazide diuretic as part of BP regimen; low dose safe in CKD stage 5

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily, titrate up to 80 mg BID as needed for congestion
medications.duration: PRN – review after 1 week then as required
medications.purpose: Manage volume overload if clinical signs of congestion (CKD stage 5, HF risk)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 recommends loop diuretic for symptomatic fluid overload; only effective at eGFR < 30

treatment_summary: The plan follows NICE CG126/NG185 for acute NSTEMI, NG106 for heart failure, and NG203/NG136 for CKD and lipid management. Dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + prasugrel) is continued for 12 months, with UFH for in‑hospital anticoagulation due to severe renal impairment. High‑intensity rosuvastatin replaces atorvastatin to achieve LDL‑C reduction, and evolocumab is added for FH‑related hypercholesterolaemia. ACE‑I dose is reduced, and atenolol is replaced by carvedilol for renal‑safe beta‑blockade. Gastro‑protection with omeprazole, blood‑pressure optimisation with amlodipine and low‑dose HCTZ, and a loop diuretic for possible congestion are included. All drug choices respect renal and hepatic constraints, avoid contraindicated agents, and incorporate monitoring per NICE guidelines.
